title: Your First Weekend at Oakland University, Shared as Cards
description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that moves from campus orientation and food to recreation, arts, and a historic campus landmark.

cards.title: Start at the Oakland Center
cards.subtitle: Find the campus gathering place
cards.notes: Begin by walking through the Oakland Center to locate meeting spaces, student-organization offices, campus services, and the food court for later.
cards.short_summary: Use the main student center as a practical first reference point.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland Center hosts conferences and events, student organization offices and meeting spaces, Pioneer Food Court, credit union, and Gear Shop.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists building hours; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Pick a lunch option at Pioneer Food Court
cards.subtitle: Oakland Center
cards.notes: Return to the Oakland Center food court when you need a meal; review the listed vendors and choose an option that fits your dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: A central campus meal stop with several named vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: Pioneer Food Court includes Grizzly Street Subs and Salads, Panda Express, The Halal Shack, and Slim Chickens.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are required; check Dine on Campus for current menus and operating hours.

cards.title: Meet at Elliott Tower
cards.subtitle: Central campus carillon plaza
cards.notes: Use the tower plaza as a campus landmark, then listen for a scheduled live carillon performance if your weekend overlaps one.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable meeting point with a 49-bell carillon.
cards.evidence_claim: Elliott Tower has a 49-bell carillon and the university lists live Friday-at-noon performances plus special-occasion concerts.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is outdoors; concert programming varies, so consult the tower page before planning around a performance.

cards.title: Settle into Kresge Library
cards.subtitle: 100 Library Drive
cards.notes: Take a short reset in the library, then identify a study room, makerspace, or research-help option you may want during the term.
cards.short_summary: The main library combines study spaces, technology, and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: Kresge Library lists group and individual study rooms, a makerspace, meeting rooms, research help, and technology services.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current hours and room-reservation rules before arrival.

cards.title: Check the OU Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: West Wilson Hall, Room 208
cards.notes: See whether an exhibition is on view, then give yourself time to walk through it; the gallery posts its regular season and hours.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery for contemporary and art-historical exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: OU Art Gallery presents contemporary and art-historical exhibitions; its events are free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists regular September–May hours and says to check for upcoming exhibitions and programming.

cards.title: Look for a Meadow Brook Theatre performance
cards.subtitle: Professional theatre on the OU campus
cards.notes: Review the current production calendar and, if a show suits your schedule, plan a ticketed evening performance with friends or family.
cards.short_summary: A professional regional theatre located on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Meadow Brook Theatre is a professional regional theatre on Oakland University's campus.
cards.access_notes: Performances and ticket availability vary; check the current theatre calendar before making plans.

cards.title: Try an activity at the Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation and Athletics Center, 569 Pioneer Drive
cards.notes: Bring appropriate athletic clothing, then check the facility schedule for open recreation, fitness areas, or a drop-in court activity.
cards.short_summary: A large campus recreation facility with fitness and court spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Recreation Center includes an indoor track, fitness center, three-court gym, activity center, studios, and racquetball courts.
cards.access_notes: Access and open-recreation availability can vary by affiliation, reservations, classes, and facility schedule.

cards.title: Walk Grizzly Oaks Disc Golf Course
cards.subtitle: East of the Recreation and Athletics Center
cards.notes: If you have discs and daylight, start at tee 1 by the tennis courts and follow the course to its finish near the northeast corner.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus disc golf course beside the outdoor recreation complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Grizzly Oaks Disc Golf Course is east of the Recreation and Athletics Center; tee 1 is by the tennis courts and tee 18 finishes near their northeast corner.
cards.access_notes: The university says the course is open to the Oakland University community; bring your own disc and use daylight-safe conditions.

cards.title: Reserve time for Meadow Brook Hall
cards.subtitle: National Historic Landmark on the OU campus
cards.notes: Check the visitor schedule and take a tour to connect the university's founding estate with its preserved architecture, rooms, and collections.
cards.short_summary: The historic Dodge Wilson estate that helped found Oakland University.
cards.evidence_claim: Meadow Brook Hall is a National Historic Landmark on Oakland University's campus; the Wilsons donated the estate and grounds to found the university.
cards.access_notes: Tour availability is schedule-dependent; Oakland University students with valid school ID are documented as receiving free tours.

cards.title: End with a meal at Hillcrest Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Hillcrest Hall
cards.notes: Close the weekend with a campus meal and an easy chance to sit together; check the current dining schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining-hall stop designed for eating and socializing.
cards.evidence_claim: Oakland University identifies Hillcrest Dining Hall as a location where students can dine and socialize.
cards.access_notes: Dining access depends on a meal plan, meal swipe, or other purchase; see Dine on Campus for current hours and menus.
